acceptanceCriteria.statement: The cockpit is drawn at the game's resolution, not the window's — its cabin, bezels and dials land on the same pixel grid as the world behind them instead of sitting on top of it sharp.

verifyVia.input: Enter HELM with Resolution set to 240p, then change it to 480p and back.
verifyVia.observable: retroRenderer.cockpitTarget.height equals the resolution setting (240, then 480), not window.innerHeight. Today it is allocated at raw window size at RetroRenderer.js:976 — the only target in resize() that skips bufferForLines().

acceptanceCriteria.statement: No text on a cockpit panel is drawn with fewer pixel rows than a letter needs to be a letter. Where the current type scale fails that, the panel is redesigned — fewer, larger rows — rather than the text being exempted from the resolution.

verifyVia.observable: Every active type tier measures at least 5 buffer pixels of cap height. A panel subtends 14.25 degrees of a 70-degree FOV, so at 240 lines it is 48.9 buffer px tall — today body (H/17) is 2.9 and label (H/20) is 2.4, both below the floor. The tier ratios are PhosphorScreen.js:195-197.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The panels still say what they need to say. Cutting rows to make the type bigger must not lose a readout the pilot actually flies with.

verifyVia.input: Fly a supercruise leg and a warp arrival with the cockpit up at 240p.
verifyVia.observable: Every value the flight loop writes to a panel is still present and legible on some panel: mode, speed, target, and the nav readouts AutopilotNavSequence drives. No field is silently dropped to make room.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The nav computer on the glass coarsens with the cabin and is still operable — it is a cockpit panel in HELM, so it cannot be exempted, and it is the surface Max steers with, so it cannot be unreadable either.

verifyVia.input: Press N in HELM at 240p, use the nav computer to pick a destination, and confirm the same flow via the mobile dock and an autopilot-initiated open.
verifyVia.observable: liveNavComputer() still resolves to the cockpit panel (main.js:5630), the panel renders at the world's resolution, its type clears the same floor as AC-2, and a destination can be selected and jumped to. The DOM fallback still appears in ORRERY.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The orbit lines match — the green ellipses stop being crisp vector strokes over a chunky world.

verifyVia.input: Sit in ORRERY at 240p with the minimap visible, then sweep Resolution 144p -> 720p.
verifyVia.observable: The rings share the world's pixel grid and stay continuous at grazing angles. The minimap's rings do not read finer than the world's at any setting — today the minimap draws into a fixed 320-square buffer, so its lines are 2.68x finer at 240p and the relationship INVERTS by 720p.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The HUD and the targeting reticle match.

verifyVia.input: Select a body in HELM and in ORRERY at 240p.
verifyVia.observable: The reticle and HUD share the world's pixel grid rather than being drawn crisp on a DOM canvas at device resolution over it.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The out-of-game harness stays sharp — the settings panel and the title screen are what Max configures the game with, and the split exists so they do not degrade.

verifyVia.input: Open the settings panel with P at 240p.
verifyVia.observable: Settings and title-screen text render as full-resolution DOM, unchanged from today. Nothing in this workstream routes them through the low-res buffer.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Nothing already accepted this session regresses.

verifyVia.input: Run the suite and the render-lines and magnitude fences.
verifyVia.observable: Buffer height still equals the resolution setting across window sizes with the aspect preserved; the star still out-reads the brightest background star; the flare glow still terminates without a black disc; the failing-test baseline is unchanged at 20 across the same 8 files.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The whole game reads as a 5th generation game.

verifyVia.input: Max flies a leg in HELM and sits in ORRERY, with the cockpit, HUD, nav computer and orbit lines all in shot.
verifyVia.observable: Max's holistic judgement that the image coheres as one fifth-generation picture rather than a 240p world with modern chrome over it. No agent renders this verdict.
